claims.statement: A Canadian border-agency audit found that built-in exact-match controls did not prevent duplicate invoices and confirmed two duplicates among ten sampled potential duplicate pairs.

A US GAO account describes recovery auditing finding millions in improper payments even after internal systems found no errors, including prevention of large duplicate wire payments; this establishes the mechanism, not a Polish recovery rate.

The ECB and EBA reported EUR 4.2 billion of EEA payment fraud in 2024 and said manipulation of payers is rising, supporting a separate bank-change and payment-anomaly check alongside duplicate detection.

contrary_evidence: Modern ERPs already implement exact duplicate checks and approval controls.
The cited recoveries are public-sector or large-enterprise examples and do not establish a Polish SME base rate.
Most algorithmic candidates can be legitimate recurring invoices, requiring costly human confirmation.

economics.acquisition_route: Offer accountants a no-recovery-no-fee audit on one closed fiscal year, require a minimum invoice count, publish anonymised precision and recovery-time results, then attach monitoring at the next payment cycle.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: One hundred fifty clients averaging 50000 PLN annual blended monitoring and recovery revenue would yield 7.5m PLN per year. A mature 40% owner-cash margin is 3m PLN annually, allowing more than 10m PLN cumulative distributions over five mature years after reinvestment and tax allowances.
economics.founder_time: Cap early audits at two concurrent clients and 3-4 hours/day, automate evidence preparation, and keep all customer recovery communication under their finance team; employment remains until stated traction and runway gates.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Export ingestion and ranking are automated, but confirmation is human-heavy initially; target 55-70% gross margin on audits and 80% or more on mature monitoring.
economics.payback: Customer payback is immediate when fees are a share of recovered cash; founder acquisition payback should be under 3 months if channel partners supply qualified datasets.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: 15-25% of cash actually recovered for the historical audit, then 1200-5000 PLN monthly by invoice volume for pre-payment monitoring; never charge on unconfirmed flags.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Payment batches recur weekly or monthly, supplier masters change and acquisitions/ERP migrations create repeat audits; retention is weak where invoice volume is small and ERP controls are mature.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A privacy-preserving library of vendor-name aliases, invoice-number transformations, credit-note patterns and adjudicated false positives improves precision without retaining customer invoices.
fingerprint.customer: Polish firms with 50-500 employees, multiple entities or branches and at least several thousand supplier invoices per year, beginning with construction and field-service groups.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Accounting firms, ERP implementers and fractional CFOs offer the audit to existing clients; construction and renewable-installation contacts provide an initial low-trust-distance segment.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Air-gapped or tightly isolated analysis of AP, payment, supplier-master and credit-note exports, with explainable candidate pairs, bank-change alerts and a recovery evidence packet; one-off contingency audit that converts to recurring pre-payment monitoring.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The CFO pays a percentage of independently confirmed recovered cash plus a fixed monitoring fee before future payment batches; the recurring loss is erroneous payment and the existing spend is AP control and audit labour.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A year-end audit, ERP migration, supplier dispute or pre-payment run creates a need to identify duplicate or erroneous disbursements that exact-match controls missed.

founder_fit: Entity resolution, fuzzy matching and anomaly ranking are a direct data-science fit.
Contingency pricing permits low-downside demand tests while the founder remains employed.
Accountants and ERP implementers can distribute a repeatable audit without continuous personal branding.
The product can remain read-only, avoiding custody of funds or authority to approve payments.
risks: False accusations could damage supplier relationships, so every flag must remain an explainable candidate for customer review.
Bank and invoice data are highly sensitive and attractive to attackers.
Contingency fees may have legal, tax or audit-independence constraints that require Polish advice.
Recovery revenue may be lumpy and fail to convert into recurring subscriptions.

structure.commercial_archetype: Contingency-fee recovery audit converting to financial-control SaaS
structure.control_point: The explainable exception queue reviewed before payment release and the evidence packet used to reclaim past overpayments
structure.critical_dependency: Complete, joinable AP/payment/supplier exports and customer cooperation in confirming and recovering flagged amounts

thesis: Run a privacy-conscious, read-only recovery audit for Polish construction, distribution and multi-entity SMEs that finds fuzzy duplicate invoices, missed credit notes, unusual bank-detail changes and contract-price mismatches, then converts repeated checks into a subscription. The CFO already loses cash to payment errors and pays ERP/accounting staff; an initial contingency fee makes demand measurable without asking the buyer to buy abstract fraud software.
title: Read-Only Accounts-Payable Recovery Audit for Mid-Market SMEs
uncertainties: The recoverable-error rate, median recovery time and supplier cooperation rate in Polish target firms are unknown.
It is untested whether accounting partners will share contingency revenue or fear exposing their own process errors.
The minimum invoice volume needed for acceptable precision and economics needs empirical calibration.
Pricing, margins, client count and founder-wealth path are assumptions.
